co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-martine.name: Monica Martinez
co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-martine.bio: Executive Director of The Fax Partnership on East Colfax for 11 years; previously worked for the City of Denver, where she helped establish its 311 service.

positions.stance: "If you live in Denver, you should get to stay in Denver. Your kids should get to grow up and build their lives here."
Champions gentle infill (duplexes, triplexes, and ADUs) to help close Denver's estimated 50,000-home housing gap.
Champions wraparound care, coordinating with Denver Health and expanding STAR's mental health response, "so leaving the streets means staying off them for good."

co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-doane-r.name: Raymon Anthony Doane
co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-doane-r.bio: Longtime Colorado public servant whose roles include budget director for the Colorado House Minority Office, tax examiner at the Department of Revenue, and property tax specialist.

positions.stance: Supports practical housing solutions, responsible growth, and neighborhood stability so Denver remains a place where working people can build a future.
Wants city government easier to understand, more transparent with taxpayer resources, and more responsive to the people it serves.
Supports investing in public safety, responsive city services, transit, and public spaces so every neighborhood feels secure and connected.
Says "clean energy and water go hand-in-hand for a resilient Denver" and that entertainment options keep the city enjoyable.
Says city government "should never serve as an obstacle to earning an honest living" and should protect small businesses' rights and opportunities.

mn-hennepin-2026-county-attorney-folk-an.name: Anders Folk
mn-hennepin-2026-county-attorney-folk-an.bio: Former U.S. Marine, federal prosecutor, and Acting U.S. Attorney for Minnesota.

positions.stance: Will be "strategic" about focusing enforcement efforts on where crime occurs and how it affects Hennepin County's diverse communities.
Will be "data-driven" in how the office intervenes to prevent harm and keep communities safe, especially the most vulnerable.
Will be "fair" in addressing juvenile justice and crime victims, and collaborative with public safety stakeholders across the county.

mn-hennepin-2026-county-attorney-frazier.name: Cedrick Frazier
mn-hennepin-2026-county-attorney-frazier.bio: DFL Minnesota State Representative and lawyer; former Hennepin County public defender, Minneapolis Public Schools legal counsel, labor attorney, and New Hope City Council member.

positions.stance: Says the office "will never work with ICE" and pledges to prosecute federal agents who violate Minnesota law.
Would create a Victim & Survivor Advisory Council on day one and offer victims optional restorative justice in select lower-level cases.
Calls ending gun violence his "top priority," with specialized prosecutors for non-fatal shootings and expanded violence intervention programs.
Pledges that charging-decision data will be "clear, easily accessible, and shared openly with the public," with regular community town halls.
Will use administrative subpoena authority against wage theft and "aggressively prosecute financial crimes" to recover what was stolen.

mn-hennepin-2026-sheriff-banks-joseph.name: Joseph Banks
mn-hennepin-2026-sheriff-banks-joseph.bio: Law enforcement officer with nearly two decades of experience.

positions.stance: Will use data-driven strategies and partnerships with local agencies to drive down violent crime with measurable results.
Promises faster investigations, clearer communication, and public reporting so residents "aren't left in the dark."
Will create regular listening sessions, increase community-based programming, and ensure deputies are visible and engaged.
Will promote diversity within the department, improve training, and build a culture of professionalism.
Will strengthen communication between city, county, and federal agencies so information flows faster during major incidents.

mn-hennepin-2026-sheriff-witt-dawanna.name: Dawanna Witt
mn-hennepin-2026-sheriff-witt-dawanna.bio: Hennepin County Sheriff, the first woman elected to the office, with more than 25 years in the Hennepin County Sheriff's Office.

positions.stance: Committed to reducing violent and property crime through data-driven partnerships with law enforcement, public health, and community groups.
Supports operational transparency, public reporting, community oversight partnerships, and policy reforms informed by community input.
Aims to address staffing shortages through aggressive hiring, competitive compensation and retention, and a diverse, well-trained workforce.

ky-jefferson-2026-mayor-parrish-wright-s.name: Shameka L. Parrish-Wright
ky-jefferson-2026-mayor-parrish-wright-s.bio: Louisville Metro Council member for District 3 since 2023 and executive director of VOCAL-KY.

positions.stance: Would expand affordable housing and tenant protections, improve grocery access, and pursue lower energy costs, including studying municipal ownership of LG&E.
Says "public safety starts with stable neighborhoods"; supports violence prevention, youth programs, and expanded mental health and addiction services.
Proposes public dashboards for spending and services, an independent accountability office, and participatory budgeting.
Supports unions, small businesses, and local jobs, career pathways for young people, and helping seniors age in place.

ky-jefferson-2026-mayor-greenberg-craig.name: Craig Greenberg
ky-jefferson-2026-mayor-greenberg-craig.bio: Mayor of Louisville since 2022; previously an attorney and entrepreneur in downtown Louisville.

positions.stance: Aims to reduce violent crime "by at least 15% each year."
"Creating good-paying jobs in every Louisville neighborhood."
Continuing "record-breaking investments in parks, libraries and public spaces."
"Building more affordable housing for families."
"Making early childhood education a reality for all 3 and 4 years olds in Louisville."

or-multnomah-2026-chair-singleton-shanno.name: Shannon Singleton
or-multnomah-2026-chair-singleton-shanno.bio: Multnomah County Commissioner for District 2 since 2024; former executive director of JOIN and interim director of the Joint Office of Homeless Services.

positions.stance: Running to bring executive experience to the Chair's Office "to ensure better service delivery in housing, addiction, behavioral health, and public safety."
Work with labor and business to create more good jobs with benefits.
Hold the County and County-funded contractors accountable for delivering effective services to the people who need them.
"Protect our immigrant friends and neighbors from ICE. Fear and intimidation have no place in our community."
"Stand up to Trump for cutting healthcare and food assistance – and threatening our fair elections."
"Reduce layers of local taxes and fees to make life in Multnomah County more affordable."

or-multnomah-2026-chair-meieran-sharon.name: Sharon Meieran
or-multnomah-2026-chair-meieran-sharon.bio: Emergency and street medicine physician and former Multnomah County Commissioner.

positions.stance: "Organizing for impact": establish a clear chain of command and a functionally integrated operational structure.
"Measuring what matters": publish transparent performance dashboards across departments.
"Budgeting for results": align budgets with measurable outcomes and redirect funding from ineffective programs.
"Accounting for every dollar" the County spends.
Within two years, a functioning homelessness-to-housing continuum with verified placement and retention outcomes.

or-multnomah-2026-auditor-pexton-nicole.name: Nicole Pexton
or-multnomah-2026-auditor-pexton-nicole.bio: Chief Audit Executive at the Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission and Certified Internal Auditor.

positions.stance: Wants quicker audits with shorter, more user-friendly reports so more services can be improved.
Develop a public report card showing what has been audited, the results, and outstanding recommendations.
Develop advisory services county departments can request to get expert audit support.

or-multnomah-2026-sheriff-morriseyodonne.name: Nicole Morrisey O'Donnell
or-multnomah-2026-sheriff-morriseyodonne.bio: Multnomah County Sheriff, elected in 2022 as the first woman in the role, with 30 years of experience.

positions.stance: Calls reducing crime her "top priority," focusing on violent crime, repeat offenders, and visible proactive law enforcement.
Supports a corrections system balancing accountability with behavioral health, education, and job readiness services to reduce recidivism.
Says "law enforcement cannot be the only solution" and will expand access to services within jails.
Will continue sharing information, reporting outcomes, and holding the office to high professional standards.
Will build relationships with community members, service providers, and partner agencies, starting with "listening and learning."

or-portland-2026-auditor-rede-simone.name: Simone Rede
or-portland-2026-auditor-rede-simone.bio: Portland City Auditor, first elected in 2022; previously a principal management auditor at Metro.

positions.stance: Maintain distance from City bureaus under review and control over the Office's budget and decisions "so that its work is credible."
Ensure City services are provided equitably and protect processes that allow people to be heard when treated unfairly.
Engage diverse people in the Office's work and communicate results in ways that build public understanding of City functions.

nv-clark-2026-treasurer-ferreira-tim.name: Tim J. "TJ" Ferreira
nv-clark-2026-treasurer-ferreira-tim.bio: Power trader in Nevada's energy market with nearly three decades in energy-market finance.

positions.stance: Automated yearly verification that the correct property-tax cap is applied to every parcel, with proactive notice of errors.
"Online everything, 24/7" for Treasurer services, while expanding in-person service hours.
Plain-language, near-real-time reporting on the county's funds, investments, and earnings; "Public dashboards are body cameras for public money."
"Prevention over punishment": clearer bills, outreach, payment plans, and returning excess tax-sale proceeds to families.
"Safety first, liquidity second, yield third," using a conservative, laddered portfolio published in plain language.

tx-bexar-2026-coa4-chief-richardson-bert.name: Bert Richardson
tx-bexar-2026-coa4-chief-richardson-bert.bio: Judge on the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals since 2015; former 379th District Court judge and Assistant U.S. Attorney.

tx-bexar-2026-coa4-chief-arteaga-antonia.name: Antonia "Toni" Arteaga
tx-bexar-2026-coa4-chief-arteaga-antonia.bio: Judge of the 57th District Court in Bexar County since 2008.

positions.stance: "I will continue to apply the law without bias, ensuring decisions are based on facts, not politics or personal beliefs."
"The Constitution and the rule of law must guide our courts"; believes in "the consistent application of legal principles."
"As Chief Justice, I will work to keep the court efficient and transparent."

tx-bexar-2026-dist-45-alvarez-mary-lou.name: Mary Lou Alvarez
tx-bexar-2026-dist-45-alvarez-mary-lou.bio: Judge of Bexar County's 45th District Court since 2018; former attorney at Texas RioGrande Legal Aid.

tx-bexar-2026-dist-144-de-leon-michael.name: Michael De Leon
tx-bexar-2026-dist-144-de-leon-michael.bio: Former Bexar County assistant district attorney and judge of Bexar County Court at Law No. 7 (2018–2022).

tx-bexar-2026-dist-150-diaz-monique.name: Monique Diaz
tx-bexar-2026-dist-150-diaz-monique.bio: Judge of the 150th Civil District Court since 2018 and adjunct professor of law at St. Mary's University.

tx-bexar-2026-dist-186-escalona-kristina.name: Kristina Escalona
tx-bexar-2026-dist-186-escalona-kristina.bio: Judge of the 186th Judicial District Court and presiding judge of the Bexar County Felony Veterans Treatment Court.

tx-bexar-2026-dist-187-franco-stephanie.name: Stephanie Franco
tx-bexar-2026-dist-187-franco-stephanie.bio: Felony prosecutor in the Bexar County District Attorney's Office.

tx-bexar-2026-dist-224-flores-marisa.name: Marisa Flores
tx-bexar-2026-dist-224-flores-marisa.bio: Presiding Judge of the 224th Civil District Court in Bexar County.

tx-bexar-2026-dist-225-robertson-benjami.name: Benjamin Robertson
tx-bexar-2026-dist-225-robertson-benjami.bio: Former civil litigator and Fourth Court of Appeals staff attorney, appointed by Gov. Abbott in 2024 to the 73rd Civil District Court.
